chunks.title: Project overview
chunks.text: Nemo is a local, API-first anonymizer for English documents. It detects personally identifiable information and redacts it. It has three detector families (regex, checksum, transformer NER), two redaction strategies (placeholder and fake), and is exposed through a REST API, the anon CLI and a Docker image. Redaction is one-way: no mapping is kept and nothing is stored server-side.

chunks.title: Supported scope
chunks.text: Nemo targets English-language text. The NER model is dslim/bert-base-NER. Regex rules follow US conventions for phone, ZIP and dates. Checksum validation is international (IBAN mod-97, Luhn for cards and French SIREN/SIRET/NIR).

chunks.title: Installation
chunks.text: Create a virtual environment and install the package in editable mode with CPU-only PyTorch: python -m venv .venv then .venv\Scripts\pip install -e ".[dev]" --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple. Requires Python 3.11 or newer.

chunks.title: Running the API locally
chunks.text: Start the FastAPI app with Uvicorn: .venv\Scripts\uvicorn anonymizer.api:app --reload. It listens on port 8000. Interactive docs are at /docs and the OpenAPI schema is at /openapi.json.

chunks.title: Regex detectors
chunks.text: Regex detectors are deterministic and fast. They emit EMAIL (user@domain.tld), PHONE (US formats such as (555) 123-4567 or +1 555 123 4567), ZIP (12345 or 12345-6789) and DATE (03/15/2024, March 15, 2024, 15 March 2024).

chunks.title: Checksum detectors
chunks.text: Checksum detectors structurally validate identifiers: IBAN with ISO 7064 mod-97, CARD numbers with Luhn (13 to 19 digits), and the French identifiers SIREN and SIRET (Luhn) and NIR (social security number, including Corsica and overseas handling). Invalid checksums are rejected, which removes false positives.

chunks.title: NER detector
chunks.text: NerDetector wraps dslim/bert-base-NER and maps PER to PERSON, ORG to ORGANIZATION, LOC to LOCATION and MISC to MISC. The backbone is capitalization-sensitive, so lowercase names like 'marcus aurelius' can be missed while 'Marcus Aurelius' is found. The model downloads on first use. In the REST API it is opt-in via ner: true.

chunks.title: Overlap resolution
chunks.text: When two entities overlap, the DetectionEngine keeps the higher-ranked span: source priority first (checksum beats regex beats ner), then longer spans, then higher confidence.

chunks.title: Entity shape
chunks.text: Every detector returns the same Entity shape: label, start, end, text, score and source. Because offsets are preserved, redaction replaces exactly the matched span.

chunks.title: Placeholder redaction
chunks.text: The default strategy replaces each entity with a stable placeholder numbered per label, such as [EMAIL_1], [EMAIL_2] and [PERSON_1]. Brackets make placeholders easy to spot when reading the redacted output.

chunks.title: Fake value redaction
chunks.text: Pass strategy=fake to replace entities with realistic surrogates generated by Faker, such as a new name, email, IBAN or card number, so the document stays readable. A caveat: a generated surrogate could coincidentally appear elsewhere in the document; plain placeholders avoid that.

chunks.title: Repeated values
chunks.text: The same (label, value) pair always receives the same replacement. 'John met John' becomes '[PERSON_1] met [PERSON_1]', which keeps relationships inside the document consistent.

chunks.title: API endpoints
chunks.text: The REST API has these endpoints: GET /health for liveness, POST /detect to return entities without changing text, POST /anonymize to redact text, POST /detect-file and POST /anonymize-file for .txt and .pdf uploads, and GET / returns the docs redirect. All request and response bodies are JSON.

chunks.title: POST /detect request
chunks.text: POST /detect takes a JSON body with text (required) and ner (optional boolean, default false). It returns an entities array of {label, start, end, text, score, source}. Setting ner true includes the transformer detector.

chunks.title: POST /anonymize request
chunks.text: POST /anonymize takes text (required), strategy (placeholder or fake, default placeholder) and ner (default false). It returns redacted text and the detected entities; nothing is stored server-side. Example body: {"text": "Email a@b.com from John Doe", "strategy": "placeholder", "ner": true}.

chunks.title: CORS configuration
chunks.text: Allowed browser origins are read from the ANONYMIZER_CORS_ORIGINS environment variable, a comma-separated list. It defaults to http://localhost:3000 for local development. Set it to your deployed frontend origin in production.

chunks.title: CLI usage
chunks.text: The CLI console is the one terminal home: run anon (or the nemo alias) with no arguments to open it (anonymize, detect, plus an engine-quickstart guide; exit with 4). Scripted use: anon detect FILE lists entities; anon anonymize FILE -o OUT [--strategy fake] writes redacted output, and a PDF input produces a redacted PDF with placeholder stamps in place (--ner/--no-ner toggles the transformer pass); -o *.pdf requires a PDF input.

chunks.title: Docker usage
chunks.text: Build the CPU-only image with docker build -t anonymizer-api . and run it with docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 anonymizer-api, or docker compose up --build. The image installs PyTorch from the CPU index so it stays small and needs no GPU. The API listens on 0.0.0.0:8000.

chunks.title: Evaluation harness
chunks.text: The eval harness generates English documents with known PII spans and reports micro-averaged precision, recall and F1. Run python -m eval.run -n 200 --seed 0. Add --ner to include the transformer model. The regex plus checksum pipeline scores 1.000 on the synthetic set by construction.

chunks.title: Limitations
chunks.text: Known limitations: NER is capitalization-sensitive and misses lowercase names; long documents are not windowed yet; regex formats target US conventions; PDF redaction needs a real text layer (scanned/image-only PDFs are rejected); redactions only remove electronic text versions and visible marks from PDFs; a fake surrogate could coincide with unrelated text; and there is no authentication or rate limiting in this build.

chunks.title: Deployment
chunks.text: Nemo is local-first. The engine runs on the user machine via the CLI console (anon or nemo), uvicorn anonymizer.api or docker compose up --build. The Next.js docs site deploys to Vercel with root directory web and only hosts documentation and the Groq-backed assistant, so it never sees your documents. The FastAPI backend cannot run on Vercel serverless because CPU PyTorch exceeds the function size limit; self-host it on Render, Railway, Fly.io or Hugging Face Spaces if you want a remote API.
